sentences.text: Revenue compounded 4.5% a year from $70.3 billion in FY2016 to $104.8 billion in FY2025 [F1][F10][F205].
The path was a step change, not a smooth climb: revenue jumped 19.8% in FY2020 and 13.3% in FY2021, then fell 1.6%, 0.8% and 1.7% in FY2023 through FY2025 [D183][D230][D324][D370][D416].
The FY2020 surge came from a 19.3% comparable sales increase and new stores, with the pandemic shifting channel and category mix [P51].
The FY2022 collapse in operating income, down 57.0% [D279], reflected discretionary category declines and markdowns taken to clear excess inventory [P38].
Operating income ended FY2025 at $5.1 billion, a 0.6% CAGR over the window, so profit barely grew while the top line compounded [F24][F207].
Food & beverage was the steady grower, rising from 19.6% of revenue in FY2017 to 23.0% in FY2025 [D484][D506].
In FY2025 food & beverage added 0.3pp to growth while apparel fell 4.7% and subtracted 0.7pp [D508][D564][D565].
FY2025 comparable sales fell 2.6%, split between a 2.2% traffic decline and a 0.4% lower average transaction [P14].
Profit grew slower than revenue in FY2025: operating income fell 8.1% against a 1.7% revenue decline [D417][D416].
Diluted EPS fell 8.2% in FY2025, slightly less than the 9.4% net income decline, as the diluted share count fell 1.3% [D420][D418][D434].
Operating margin was 4.9% in FY2025, below the 5.6% window median and far under the 8.4% FY2021 high [F34][D590][D589].
The FY2025 margin slipped 0.3pp, with cost of revenue taking 0.3pp and SG&A adding 0.1pp [D429][D440][D441].
The SG&A rate held at 20.6% only because a 0.6pp interchange settlement benefit offset deleveraging from lower sales [P11].
Gross margin fell to 27.9% from 28.2%, and the filing attributes the decrease to the net impact of several factors it does not itemise in the quoted passage [P12].
The tax rate was 22.3% in FY2025 against 22.2% in FY2024, so net margin tracked operating margin rather than diverging [D403][D357].
Operating cash flow of $6.6 billion was 1.77x net income in FY2025, below the 2.17x FY2019 level [F84][F44][D404][D124].
The FY2025 decline reflected lower net earnings plus lower accounts payable leverage and inventory purchases [P7].
Free cash flow fell 36.7% to $2.8 billion, a 2.7% margin against the 4.5% window median [F104][D422][D401][D596].
Capex rose 28.9% to $3.7 billion, 1.19x D&A, on increased investment in new stores and remodels [F94][D423][D406][P5].
Net debt was $4.3 billion, or 4.1% of revenue, against a retail peer median of -3.5% net cash and at the 50th percentile of six peers [D410][D411][D613][D612].
Cash and investments reached $10.1 billion against $14.4 billion of debt, and the current ratio was 0.94x, at its window median [D408][D409][F184][D602].
Buybacks plus dividends of $2.5 billion absorbed 86.8% of free cash flow in FY2025, with repurchases cut to $408 million [D412][D413][X126].
The diluted share count fell from 582.5 million in FY2016 to 455.6 million in FY2025, which is why EPS compounded 6.3% against 3.4% net income growth [X107][X116][F210][F208].
Revenue has now declined three years running, from $109.1 billion in FY2022 to $104.8 billion in FY2025 [F7][F8][F9][F10][R1].
The latest year's decline came from lower traffic and transaction size, with discretionary categories the weak spot [P14][P30].
The current ratio of 0.94x sits below 1.0x, though it matches the window median and is above the 0.83x FY2018 low [F184][D602][D600][R2].
The 2.4-year burn coverage flag [R3] is stale: it refers to the FY2022 free cash flow deficit of $1.5 billion, and free cash flow has been positive in every year since [D276][F101][F102][F103][F104].
Operating margin has fallen two years in a row, 0.4pp in total, to 4.9% [F32][F33][F34][R4].
Watch whether operating margin holds above the 3.5% FY2022 low; a break below it would confirm the margin erosion is structural [D588].
Watch capex against the roughly $5 billion FY2026 guidance; spending at that level against FY2025's $3.7 billion would keep free cash flow margin under the 4.5% median [P4][F94][D596].
Watch whether revenue stops falling; a return to growth would reverse the three-year decline, reported in the FY2026 10-K [F10][R1].
